name: Sam Altman
thesis: Build the whole abundance stack in dependency order: cheap energy first, then intelligence, then biology and the interface between them. Holds no OpenAI equity — the portfolio is the fortune.

name: Jeff Bezos
thesis: The most active family office in private markets in 2026. Applies AI to atoms — manufacturing, robotics, cars, biology, minerals — and has moved from writing cheques to running an AI company himself.

name: Elon Musk
thesis: Does not diversify; concentrates entirely in companies he controls. With SpaceX public and xAI folded into it, his private surface has narrowed to the brain interface and the tunnels.

name: Peter Thiel
thesis: Contrarian concentration — a small number of enormous cheques into things that look like monopolies-in-waiting. Was early to defence, fusion and prediction markets before any were consensus.

name: Palmer Luckey
thesis: Builds the institutions his own sector is denied. A defence prime, then a chartered bank for companies traditional banks won't underwrite, then the reactors to power them.

name: Vinod Khosla
thesis: Funds science experiments, with fund mandates written explicitly for fusion, humanoids and autonomous systems. Leaning toward applied and physical AI over another model lab.

name: Eric Schmidt
thesis: Went from funding the frontier to operating it — took the chief executive seat at a launch company and is arguing compute should move to orbit.

name: Patrick Collison
thesis: Backs the layer everyone else builds on, plus the scientific institutions that produce the discoveries in the first place. Long horizons, very few positions.

name: Jensen Huang
thesis: The most systemic investor on the board — personally signs off every deal, and holds across nearly every theme because every theme buys his chips.

name: Friedman & Gross
thesis: Taste-makers of the AI seed market. Their conviction tends to precede consensus by roughly eighteen months, and where they follow on is more informative than where they enter.

name: Reid Hoffman
thesis: Network-effect businesses for two decades, now betting personally that AI collapses drug discovery — and left the Microsoft board in June 2026 to go run it himself.

name: Brian Armstrong
thesis: Co-founded a longevity company with nothing to do with crypto, on the thesis that epigenetic reprogramming is the highest-leverage problem money can currently be pointed at.

name: Josh Kushner
thesis: Extreme concentration into perceived category winners at prices that look indefensible until they aren't. Now writing billion-dollar cheques into fusion and robots, not just software.

name: Marc Andreessen
thesis: Turned national-interest investing into an explicit fund thesis — defence, manufacturing, energy, housing — and captured an outsized share of all US venture dollars doing it.

name: Elad Gil
thesis: The largest one-person fund in the market. Currently telling his own AI founders to take exits inside twelve to eighteen months, which is itself a signal worth reading.

name: Joe Lonsdale
thesis: Backs 'national capability' — defence, industrials, bio-infrastructure — framed as an American industrial renaissance, and moved the firm to Texas to make the point.

name: Bill Gates
thesis: The longest-horizon capital on the board. Funds the unglamorous physical substrate — reactors, geothermal, mineral discovery — on twenty-year timelines nobody else underwrites.

name: Masayoshi Son
thesis: Has put roughly 60% of SoftBank's assets into what he calls ASI-oriented positions, and names physical AI and 'robots manufacturing robots' as the next trillion-dollar opportunity.

name: Daniel Ek
thesis: The most consequential European operator-investor. Seeded a defence champion and a preventive-health company, and chairs the former — an explicitly sovereignty-flavoured book.

name: Naval Ravikant
thesis: Very early, very broad, very small cheques. Sixteen unicorns from a portfolio built on judging founders rather than markets.

name: Tobi Lütke
thesis: Invests where he has operator scar tissue — commerce, developer tooling, and the security layer under AI applications. Forty-three positions, six exits.

name: Dylan Field
thesis: Ninety angel positions concentrated in the creative and developer tool layer, with an unusually high exit rate for a founder investing on the side.

name: Jack Dorsey
thesis: The board's only true ideological investor. Funds protocols and open-source commons rather than equity, on the view that owning the rails is the wrong goal.

name: Brian Chesky
thesis: Deliberately tiny book. Invests only where he can be operationally useful, mostly design-led consumer and housing, and says no far more than yes.

name: Garry Tan
thesis: Sits at the widest funnel in the market. His signal is less about any one cheque than about which categories keep reappearing in successive YC batches.

name: Andrej Karpathy
thesis: Eighteen positions, weighted toward the silicon and tooling beneath models rather than the models themselves. Joined Anthropic's pretraining team in 2026.

name: Ilya Sutskever
thesis: Raised seven billion dollars for a company with no product, no revenue and no published research, on the single proposition that superintelligence should be built safety-first or not at all.

name: Mira Murati
thesis: Left the OpenAI CTO seat and raised one of the largest seed rounds in history. The bet is that frontier capability walks out of the door with the people, not the org chart.

name: Yann LeCun
thesis: Left Meta to build world models on the explicit argument that language models are a dead end for real intelligence. The most senior person on the board betting against the prevailing architecture.

name: Fei-Fei Li
thesis: The researcher behind ImageNet, now arguing spatial intelligence is the missing primitive — that a model which cannot represent a persistent 3D world cannot reason about reality.

name: Bret Taylor
thesis: Chairs the board of the second-most valuable private company while building the agent layer that would sit on top of it. Pricing agents on outcomes rather than seats.

name: Aravind Srinivas
thesis: Running the most direct frontal assault on Google search of the last twenty years, and the company most widely co-held by individual operators on this board.

name: Baiju Bhatt
thesis: Left a retail brokerage to beam solar power from orbit to ground receivers. One of the few genuinely pre-consensus physical bets a successful founder has taken with their own money.

name: Demis Hassabis
thesis: Quietly angel-funded the labs that became his own competitors, including an early cheque into Anthropic, while building the drug-design company inside his own house.

name: Arthur Mensch
thesis: Europe's answer to the frontier labs, built on open weights and data sovereignty. The clearest live test of whether sovereignty is a real moat or a procurement preference.

name: Liang Wenfeng
thesis: Put roughly $2.95B of his own money in to stay the largest holder, and structured the round so outside investors got virtually no voting rights, no board seats and a five-year lock-up. Says he will only pursue AGI — explicitly rejecting the ByteDance and Tencent commercial path.

name: Wang Xingxing
thesis: Cleared China's STAR Market listing review as the first embodied-AI company to do so, and is targeting ten to twenty thousand humanoid units shipped in 2026 — roughly the entire Western sector's ambition, already in production.

name: Zhang Yiming
thesis: China's richest founder, running the largest still-private consumer tech company in the world while pushing ByteDance's own frontier models. Invests almost entirely inside his own perimeter.

name: Neil Shen
thesis: The single most important allocator in Chinese venture, and the main bridge routing non-Chinese capital into China's AI push after HongShan's 2023 split from Sequoia.

name: Kai-Fu Lee
thesis: Argues China wins on deployment economics rather than research firsts — cheaper models, faster productisation. Taking 01.AI toward a Hong Kong listing.

name: Yang Zhilin
thesis: Building Kimi into China's fastest-scaling AI revenue story on an open-weight strategy, having raised three times in six months at rapidly escalating prices.

name: Wang Xing
thesis: The most active operator-backer inside China's private AI and robotics stack, funding model labs and humanoid companies from an operating company's balance sheet.

name: He Xiaopeng
thesis: Running the widest hardware spread of anyone here — electric cars, humanoid robots and eVTOL aircraft from one engineering base, on the view that they are the same robotics problem.

name: Nikhil Kamath
thesis: India's most visible operator-investor, funding climate, health and fintech domestically at a moment when four of five new ventures from major Indian founders carry an explicit deep-tech mandate.

name: Xavier Niel
thesis: Bankrolled the infrastructure that made a French frontier lab possible at all. Invests in European technological independence as a political project, not only a financial one.

name: Alexandr Wang
thesis: Built the data layer the frontier labs trained on, then sold into Meta's superintelligence effort. A small, sharply concentrated personal book aimed at agentic research.

name: Trae Stephens
thesis: Palantir's early employee, then a Founders Fund partner, then co-founder of Anduril — and he holds the executive chairmanship while still investing. The single clearest carrier of the Palantir-to-Anduril lineage that produced most of the defence theme on this board.

name: Lux Capital
thesis: The most literary of the hard-tech funds. Backs founders working at the edge of physics, biology and defence, and has been in Anduril, Varda, Impulse and Physical Intelligence early enough to shape them.

name: Playground Global
thesis: Partners with technical and scientific founders from next-generation compute through engineered biology. Its silicon book — Ayar, d-Matrix, xLight, Snowcap — is the deepest bet on post-NVIDIA hardware anywhere on this board.

name: Eclipse Ventures
thesis: Invests exclusively in the physical industries — manufacturing, logistics, construction, defence — on the thesis that the digital economy is done and the atoms economy is the opportunity.

name: DCVC
thesis: Backs deep tech aimed at trillion-dollar problems, with an unusually long tail across climate, computational biology and industrial AI. Over four hundred companies, most of them invisible.

name: Root Ventures
thesis: Writes the first cheque into engineering-hard companies — robotics, manufacturing, semiconductors, scientific tooling. The earliest-stage fund here and therefore the best leading indicator of what the larger funds will price in two years.

name: Tencent
thesis: The most consequential single backer in Chinese deep tech — on the cap table of Unitree, AgiBot, DeepSeek, Moonshot, StepFun and Enflame simultaneously.

name: Alibaba
thesis: Backs the model labs and the robotics companies that will run on its cloud. Also the largest external holder in several BCI and humanoid names.

name: HongShan
thesis: The most important allocator in Chinese venture and the main bridge routing non-Chinese capital into China's AI and robotics push.

name: IDG Capital
thesis: The longest-running foreign-origin fund in China, now deeply embedded in the humanoid and eVTOL cohorts.

name: Hillhouse
thesis: Crossover capital at the late-stage end of Chinese deep tech, increasingly into embodied AI.

name: Chinese state funds
thesis: Not one investor but a class. National, provincial and municipal vehicles anchor a large share of Chinese deep-tech rounds — where they lead, the valuation reflects industrial policy and land subsidy rather than a competitive auction. Treat it as a different instrument from a private cheque.

name: Temasek
thesis: The most globally distributed sovereign investor here — present in Israeli security, Indian space, Dutch semiconductors and Chinese biotech.

name: GIC
thesis: Quieter than Temasek and later-stage. Co-led India's first spacetech unicorn.

name: Mubadala
thesis: Controls G42 and appears across AI infrastructure globally. The Gulf's principal instrument for buying a position in the compute layer.

name: PIF
thesis: Creates national champions by decree rather than backing founders — HUMAIN and Neo Space Group were established, not funded. Programme spend, not venture.

name: NATO Innovation Fund
thesis: Nineteen portfolio companies from a $1.1B mandate. Its presence is the clearest signal that a European defence company has cleared an alliance-level credibility bar.

name: British Business Bank
thesis: Committed £100M to a single quantum round — its largest reported startup commitment — alongside positions in autonomy and maritime defence.

name: Bpifrance
thesis: The state as anchor investor in French sovereignty plays: Mistral, Pasqal, Alice & Bob. Often paired with defence-procurement programmes.

name: EU state funds
thesis: German, Spanish and EU-level vehicles now anchor rounds that private European capital will not lead alone. In some cases — Black Semiconductor — the state money is the overwhelming majority of a headline figure.

name: Indian sovereign funds
thesis: Structurally new. India's state moved from customer to equity investor in 2025–26: the Antariksh space fund wrote its first cheque, the National Quantum Mission co-led a Series A, and Tamil Nadu put direct equity into a launch company.

name: Sequoia Capital
thesis: Post-split Sequoia is a US and European fund. Co-led the largest European loitering-munitions round, which is not a sentence anyone would have written five years ago.

name: Lightspeed
thesis: One of the few funds present in fusion, defence, Indian AI and Chinese robotics simultaneously.

name: General Catalyst
thesis: Has moved decisively into European defence and Indian drones — an explicit bet that the next decade of returns is geopolitical.

name: Balderton
thesis: Europe's most consistent deep-tech Series A investor, now co-leading orbital capsules and autonomous driving.

name: Atomico
thesis: Skype-lineage fund that helped define European venture; now weighted toward hard tech and sovereignty.

name: Plural
thesis: Founder-operators investing in European hard tech — the closest structural analogue to the US operator-investor model this dataset was built to track.

name: HV Capital
thesis: German deep-tech mainstay across launch, defence robotics and semiconductors.

name: Japanese state funds
thesis: Japan's state is the anchor investor in its own reindustrialisation. IPA holds a golden share in Rapidus with a right to seize control on distress; NEDO, JIC and the policy banks appear across chips, fusion, space and autonomy. Closer to industrial policy than venture.

name: Australian state funds
thesis: Government money is the dominant force in Australian deep tech, not a supplement to it. The National Reconstruction Fund appears in eight of eighteen companies researched and CSIRO's Main Sequence in nine. Australia's problem is not early capital — it is that scale-ups leave, as PsiQuantum did.

name: NZ state funds
thesis: Small but decisive at the earliest stage. The Regional Development Fund's NZ$35m loan to OpenStar is the largest state commitment to a private New Zealand deep-tech company on this board.

name: Korean state funds
thesis: Korea's ₩150tn National Growth Fund has named AI compute and solid-state batteries as first-priority sectors. Korea Development Bank sits on most of the significant AI-silicon cap tables. This money is likely to reprice several Korean names within a year.
